evidence_quotes.quote: O presente artigo tem como objetivo apresentar um panorama da tarifa social no Brasil e verificar como as diferentes formas de prestação do serviço influenciam: (i) a incidência da tarifa social, em termos do número de municípios que apresentam o benefício; (ii) o alcance social da tarifação social, em termos do número de potenciais usuários de fato beneficiados; e (iii) o comprometimento da renda dos beneficiários.

evidence_quotes.page: Section 2.1. Construção do panorama da tarifação social no Brasil
evidence_quotes.quote: Um panorama da tarifa social no Brasil foi elaborado a partir do levantamento e sistematização de dados do Sistema Nacional de Informações sobre Saneamento (SNIS) e do sistema de Consulta, Seleção e Extração de Informações do CadÚnico, ambos referentes ao ano de 2021.

evidence_quotes.page: Section 4.3 Critérios de enquadramento na tarifa social
evidence_quotes.quote: A análise de correlação de Spearman mostrou que o número de critérios de enquadramento na tarifa social e o percentual de economias beneficiadas em relação aos cadastrados no CadÚnico apresentam relação estatisticamente significativa (p-valor = 0,018) e apresentam correlação negativa moderada (ρ = -0,521).

evidence_quotes.page: Section 4.2.2 Economias beneficiadas com tarifa social em relação à quantidade de famílias inscritas no CadÚnico
evidence_quotes.quote: Verificou-se que 14,6% das famílias inscritas no CadÚnico com acesso à rede de distribuição de água tem acesso ao benefício da tarifa social no Brasil.

evidence_quotes.page: Section 4.4 Comprometimento da renda dos usuários na tarifa social
evidence_quotes.quote: Considerando uma família com renda de um salário mínimo, tem-se que os únicos cinco prestadores que apresentam tarifa social média que supera 3% do salário mínimo vigente na época são privados.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines economic access (affordability and social-tariff benefit access) to household drinking-water supply and water-and-sewage services across Brazil.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Under the plain wording, the study analyses tariff regulation, social-tariff policies under Federal Law No. 11.445/2007, and water/sanitation institutional service delivery models. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, it directly examines three core rule-type mechanisms governing household economic access and exclusion: (1) tariff and subsidy rules (social tariff structures and price levels), (2) eligibility screening rules and documentation/administrative burden (number and types of eligibility criteria such as housing construction characteristics, CadÚnico registration, proof of income, Bolsa Família, and electricity consumption), and (3) utility ownership and corporate governance structure (local/microregional public vs. private providers, and regional public, private, closed-capital mixed-economy, and open-capital mixed-economy utilities) governing social-tariff incidence, benefit coverage, and affordability.
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical quantitative cross-sectional study analysing 2021 administrative micro/provider-level data from Brazil's Sistema Nacional de Informações sobre Saneamento (SNIS) and Cadastro Único (CadÚnico), employing descriptive statistics, thematic mapping (ArcGIS), and Spearman non-parametric correlation analysis.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports multiple relevant service-access, affordability, and exclusion outcomes: (i) municipal incidence of social tariffs, (ii) social-tariff coverage/exclusion as the percentage of total active connections (economias) and of low-income CadÚnico-registered families with water network access receiving the social tariff, and (iii) affordability measured as mean social tariff price and percentage of a 2021 minimum-wage household income relative to the UN 3% benchmark.
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies population and units of analysis (Brazilian water and water-and-sewage service providers excluding direct public administration and sewage-only providers, municipalities, 27 federative units, household water connections/economias, and CadÚnico-registered families with water network access in 2021), exposures (utility ownership/service delivery model and number/type of social-tariff eligibility criteria), outcomes (social-tariff incidence, coverage, and income commitment/affordability), and study design (cross-sectional quantitative observational analysis of administrative datasets).
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese (with Portuguese and English abstracts), which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

study_design: Quantitative cross-sectional observational study using national administrative datasets (SNIS and CadÚnico, 2021) with descriptive statistics, thematic GIS mapping, and Spearman rank correlation analysis.
population_and_sample: Brazilian water supply and water-and-sewage service providers (excluding direct public administration and sewage-only providers), municipalities, all 27 Brazilian federative units (UFs), active household connections (economias), and low-income families registered in CadÚnico with access to the water distribution network in 2021.
exposure: Water and sanitation utility ownership/service delivery model (local/microregional public vs. private; regional public, private, closed-capital mixed-economy, and open-capital mixed-economy companies) and social-tariff eligibility screening criteria (number and types of eligibility rules).
outcome: Municipal incidence of social tariffs; social-tariff coverage (% of total active connections/economias and % of CadÚnico-registered low-income families with water network access receiving the social tariff); and tariff affordability (mean social tariff level and % commitment of a 2021 minimum-wage household income relative to the 3% UN benchmark).
rationale: This Portuguese-language full-text empirical study meets all inclusion criteria (c1–c6). Using 2021 national administrative data from SNIS and CadÚnico across Brazil, it empirically evaluates rule-type legal, regulatory, and institutional mechanisms directly governing economic access to water and sanitation services—specifically utility ownership/delivery structure, social-tariff pricing rules, and eligibility screening criteria/documentation requirements—against concrete access, exclusion, and affordability outcomes (municipal social-tariff availability, coverage of active connections and CadÚnico low-income households, and share of minimum-wage income spent on social tariffs, including a Spearman correlation linking stricter multi-criteria eligibility rules to lower low-income household coverage).
